CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain. Patient reports injury occurred on Sunday, approximately 4 days ago while skiing. She was attempting moguls when her ski strap became caught on her finger, causing hyperextension of the finger. Patient has attempted conservative management with ice application and ibuprofen without significant improvement. Pain is exacerbated by movement. Denies any other associated symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports recent constipation. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation (recent)
Appendectomy at age 18

MEDICATIONS
Miralax

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational skiing

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right hand exam reveals tenderness over the distal phalanx. Tenderness present over the distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over the proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Patient able to flex and extend finger. Patient able to touch thumb with affected finger. Pain noted with flexion.

RESULTS
X-rays of right hand: Normal with no fractures identified. Good alignment of bones.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right hand index finger contusion of the tip of the finger with no fracture. Patient to wear aluminum foam splint. Ibuprofen 600 mg orally every 6 hours for approximately one week. Patient instructed to call and return to clinic if symptoms do not improve.
